note: An analytical organisation for this survey. It is not the architecture of any commercial model and is not claimed as the first such taxonomy.

stages.label: Decision contract
stages.question: What exactly is being asked, and what may the answer be?
stages.covers: State, typed question, option names, rubrics, levels, cardinality, abstain options.
stages.evidence: Type validity; name and order invariance; closed-set failure when the right option is missing.

stages.label: Inference & readout
stages.question: How is a distribution over the declared options produced?
stages.covers: Hosted service, encoder heads, frozen or fine-tuned decoder readouts, diffusion reads, generative adapters.
stages.evidence: Same-backbone ablations; readout geometry; what is and is not disclosed.

stages.label: Probability & calibration
stages.question: What does a returned probability or confidence mean, and for which population?
stages.covers: Native vs verbalised probabilities, confidence statistics, ECE/Brier/NLL, recalibration, quantisation.
stages.evidence: Per-task reliability, high-confidence errors, recalibration on held-out labels.

stages.label: Selective control
stages.question: When should software act, ask, escalate or abstain?
stages.covers: Thresholds, risk–coverage, cascades to stronger models, human review budgets.
stages.evidence: Coverage at fixed risk; escalation rate; thresholds chosen on a separate selection set.

stages.label: Downstream use
stages.question: Does the whole workflow get better, cheaper or faster?
stages.covers: End-task success, end-to-end latency, cost per correct completion, derived quantities.
stages.evidence: System-level baselines; module attribution; matched measurement scope.

method_families.label: Hosted System One service
method_families.principle: A closed, hosted model returns a distribution over declared options for each typed question about a shared text state.
method_families.disclosed: Interface, primitives, pricing, limits, versioning and known failure modes are documented; architecture, training data and the exact confidence statistic are not.
method_families.boundary: Black-box evaluation only; the served model can change behind aliases; text-only input.

method_families.label: Encoder decision heads
method_families.principle: A bidirectional encoder reads state, question and options together; a head scores each option and a softmax is taken over the legal set.
representatives: open marker-readout and span-mean heads audited in 2609.26758
method_families.disclosed: Weights and inference code for Laya; the readout geometry (marker token vs span mean) changes name sensitivity.
method_families.boundary: Short context windows; option-name polarity can dominate the rubric; adjacent to GLiClass, SetFit and NLI zero-shot classifiers.

method_families.label: Frozen decoder option readout
method_families.principle: An unmodified causal LM is prompted once and the next-token logits of single-token option labels are renormalised over the declared options.
method_families.disclosed: Fully open and training-free; the natural low-cost baseline for any trained decision model.
method_families.boundary: Raw logits are order-sensitive and poorly calibrated without correction; label tokenisation matters.

method_families.label: Fine-tuned decoder decision models
method_families.principle: A decoder is adapted (LoRA or full fine-tuning) so that a designated position or pointer head yields calibrated option probabilities in one pass.
method_families.disclosed: Several release weights, training code and evaluation data; lineages exist (this-that-model is adapted from decider-2b).
method_families.boundary: Gains may come from task coverage in training; derived checkpoints are not independent methods.

method_families.label: Diffusion structured readout
method_families.principle: A discrete diffusion LM is seeded with the answer template; after one denoising step, the distribution at each answer slot is read directly.
method_families.disclosed: Open servers with a Jev-compatible wire API; depends on request extensions proposed in an unmerged vLLM PR.
method_families.boundary: A different mechanism from last-token decoder readout; custom entropy-based confidence.

method_families.label: Generative & constrained adapters
method_families.principle: A general LLM is asked (often under JSON-schema constraints) to emit a decision and probabilities, which are validated and returned in Jev-shaped responses.
method_families.disclosed: Wire compatibility for controlled comparisons; probabilities are generated or verbalised, not read from logits.
method_families.boundary: Interface compatibility is not mechanism equivalence; retries, parsing and self-reported probabilities remain.

findings.title: A type-valid answer can still be the wrong answer.
findings.body: Typed interfaces remove parse and schema failures by construction. They say nothing about whether the model read the option the way the author intended: rebinding option names to rubrics, removing an abstain option or asking through a different primitive can move answers while the type-error rate stays at zero.

findings.title: A native probability makes calibration measurable, not guaranteed.
findings.body: Every call returns a distribution, so reliability can be audited on each run. Measured calibration varies by task and construct, confident errors occur, probabilities are quantised to two decimals, and recalibration fitted on in-distribution labels helps substantially. Calibration is a property to verify per workload, not a certificate.

findings.title: The most consistent use is a bounded first pass with confidence-gated escalation.
findings.body: Across judging, annotation and agent control, the typed model is usually cheaper and faster but not the most accurate component. Gains appear when uncertain cases are routed to a stronger model or a person, thresholds are chosen on separate data, and cheap generative cascades are included as baselines.

findings.title: Speed and cost claims decompose into different mechanisms and scopes.
findings.body: Single-request latency, per-question amortized time, batch throughput, end-to-end task time, simulated timing, electricity-only cost and API bills are different quantities. Prefix sharing, batching and caching can explain as much as the readout does. None of the figures can be pooled into a single leaderboard.

findings.title: Interface compatibility is not mechanism equivalence.
findings.body: Open projects reproduce the request and response shape with encoders, frozen or fine-tuned decoders, diffusion reads or prompted generators. Their probabilities come from different mechanisms, they differ in what is released, and none establishes the architecture of the commercial model.

findings.title: System-level gains need module-level attribution and the right reference.
findings.body: Memory systems, orchestration pipelines and scientific workflows improve for many reasons at once. Attribution requires ablations, matched baselines and references that measure what the workflow reuses (derived quantities, narrative-grounded labels) rather than only final labels.

findings.title: The evidence base is young, clustered and unreplicated.
findings.body: Thirteen core preprints appeared within four days, each as a single version; two share a study family; many community results are self-reported; several comparisons rest on a handful of items or on test-set-informed choices. None of the core results has been independently reproduced.

failure_modes.title: Option name outweighs the rubric
failure_modes.desc: Rebinding which rubric sits behind “no/yes” moves answers far more than the same swap behind neutral names; a 0% type-error rate hides it.
failure_modes.mitigation: Neutral identifiers with meaning carried in the rubric; name-invariance checks next to type-error rates.

failure_modes.title: Order is a different intervention
failure_modes.desc: Reordering options and rebinding names test different things: one community audit found no argmax flips under order changes on hosted Jev, while frozen open readouts are order-sensitive until calibrated.
failure_modes.mitigation: Report order permutation and name rebinding as separate arms.

failure_modes.title: The primitive changes the answer
failure_modes.desc: A Noul and a two-option Choice over the same question can disagree, and the choice of primitive can reverse a comparison with an LLM baseline.
failure_modes.mitigation: Fix the primitive in a protocol; test both when a result depends on it.

failure_modes.title: Forced choice without an exit
failure_modes.desc: When the correct answer is not among the options, a typed model must still choose; removing an abstain option collapsed accuracy on unanswerable items at high confidence.
failure_modes.mitigation: Include an explicit unknown/abstain option and test with it removed.

failure_modes.title: Confident on the wrong construct
failure_modes.desc: Calibration varies by task: on one construct the model was confident while near chance, and audits disagree across datasets.
failure_modes.mitigation: Audit reliability per task and construct, not with one global ECE.

failure_modes.title: Unknowable rules and distribution shift
failure_modes.desc: On labels not recoverable from the text, probabilities stayed concentrated; a large post-hoc temperature was needed to make them honest.
failure_modes.mitigation: Hold out domains and rule changes; recalibrate on target-domain labels.

failure_modes.title: Language shift costs accuracy
failure_modes.desc: A Spanish state with English instructions lost accuracy on every tested dataset; calibration worsened on the hardest tasks.
failure_modes.mitigation: Evaluate in the deployment language; pin the model version.

failure_modes.title: Two-decimal probabilities
failure_modes.desc: Probabilities are returned on a 0.01 grid, which puts a floor under calibration error for rare events and can place exactly zero on a correct answer.
failure_modes.mitigation: Treat rare-event probabilities with care; smooth before log-loss.

failure_modes.title: Same request, different answer
failure_modes.desc: Repeated identical requests to the hosted model do not always return the same answer, which sets a floor under any flip-rate comparison.
failure_modes.mitigation: Measure a test–retest floor and report effects relative to it.

failure_modes.title: Validity effects masquerade as quality
failure_modes.desc: When comparing with generative baselines, parse failures and repairs change accuracy independently of reasoning; typed outputs remove the failure but not the confound in comparisons.
failure_modes.mitigation: Count invalid outputs as errors and report parse rates separately.

failure_modes.title: Right label, wrong quantity
failure_modes.desc: A wrong intermediate selection can change a derived count while leaving the final label correct.
failure_modes.mitigation: Score intermediate relations and derived quantities, not only final labels.

failure_modes.title: Vendor-listed jagged edges
failure_modes.desc: The vendor lists literal reading, arithmetic and counting, date comparison, indirection, large irrelevant state, adversarial content and contradictory criteria as known weaknesses.
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep arithmetic and date logic in code; filter state; split indirect questions.

application_cards.decides: Which of two responses is better, or whether an answer is supported.
application_cards.caution: Derivation checking and style-adversarial pairs remain hard; adjudication by one author.

application_cards.decides: Labels for social-science text and crash narratives, with a probability per label.
application_cards.caution: Per-construct failures; recalibration fitted on in-distribution labels.

application_cards.decides: Which tool or action to take next inside an agent, escalating to a strong LLM when unsure.
application_cards.caution: A cheap generative cascade is competitive where routing is already accurate.

application_cards.decides: How memories are typed, routed, budgeted, traversed and when retrieval stops.
application_cards.caution: System-level gains with a different baseline per number; LLM-judge metric.

application_cards.decides: Which scientific relation governs a calculation that code then performs.
application_cards.caution: Twenty Choices in ten cases; not discriminative across strong models.

application_cards.decides: A quality level from extracted metadata, bitstream and pixel features — never from the video itself.
application_cards.caution: Trained models on the same features remain ahead.

application_cards.decides: Whether a call is a scam, after every caller turn (open JevLite model).
application_cards.caution: Synthetic callers; recipe selected with test-set exposure.

application_cards.decides: Bounded intent fields and service contracts for an edge scheduler.
application_cards.caution: One study family; caching largely removes the latency gap.

application_cards.decides: Several forced-choice questions about one image (independent Visual Jev model).
application_cards.caution: Amortized timing; gains concentrated on trained task families.
